items_missed: Set the Agenda: no upfront agenda statement (what he'd cover + rough time) and no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before diving into intake questions.
Probe: never captured zip codes for either the origin or destination address; didn't ask about storage needs or any additional stops.
Pricing: skipped the 'pricing is super simple' opener before launching into the rate breakdown.
Estimate: dismissed the destination's six steps as fee-irrelevant without tying stairs into the time estimate itself; no walk-distance or equivalents (school bus, etc.) framing used.
Save Your Ass: delivered the prep-and-consolidate message well but never gave the explicit 'take a carload' tip.

Quote/Booking: no 'no deposit required' mention, no bolded-key-details framing described for the email, no explicit 'reply with any corrections' verification ask, and no hours/how-to-reach-us info given.
Bonus: mostly one-directional transactional delivery with little humor or two-way rapport, plus a self-corrected stumble transitioning into pricing ('I got a little twisted up there').
top_strength: Khevan's pricing and estimate walkthrough was excellent and fully transparent — he proactively explained the drive-time logic for adding a third mover ('with that, I would want to allocate a third mover just to make the short in the day') and gave a clean no-hidden-fees pitch: 'there are no additional or hidden fees... no fees of any type.'
coaching_note: Open every call with a real agenda statement and a 'sound good?' before you start pulling info — right now you jump straight from name to move date with no framing. Capture zip codes on both addresses every time, and ask about storage and additional stops even when the answer is probably no. On the close, explicitly say no deposit is required and ask 'any other questions before I let you go?' with your hours — you got Danny thinking about booking but didn't hand him every reason to feel confident doing it today. Also tighten the handoff into your pricing pitch; you called yourself out mid-call for getting twisted up, and a smoother transition will sound more polished.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and used Danny's name repeatedly with a warm close, but the call ran mostly as a one-directional monologue with a monosyllabic customer and little genuine back-and-forth rapport.
